findings.what: One stated service period is frozen into the plan revision's basis, so every occurrence of a multi-period schedule posts a journal line describing the SAME term — including occurrences whose posting date precedes that term. There is no congruence wall between the stated term and the effective window: the term may sit wholly outside it and the schedule may be open-ended.
findings.evidence: Probe C on the fresh chain (clara_652r): configured effective_from=2026-06-01, effective_to=null, monthly/last_day_of_month, stated term 2026-07-01..2026-07-31, then catch-up + post. Three primary entries: posting=2026-06-30, 2026-07-31, 2026-08-31 — each with lines [{acct 6100, dr 120000, desc "accrued 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31"},{acct 2020, cr 120000, desc "accrual"}]. So a July term is debited in June and again in August, and the ledger text is false on two of the three entries. Probe C2: an accrual whose term is 2031-01-01..2031-12-31 on an effective window of one month was ACCEPTED (accrual 808fc28c-3378-4b66-8b02-54ca661dcd2f). Cents, accounts and posting dates are correct throughout (dr=cr=120000 on all three).
findings.fix: In clara._assert_accrual_particulars / the two doors, refuse a configuration whose stated term is not bracketed by the authority window (CLR10 accrual_term_window_mismatch, field accrual.service_period_start/end), AND refuse a schedule that would generate more than one primary occurrence while carrying a single fixed term (require effective_to, and require the schedule to yield exactly one primary due date for the stated-term methods). If a recurring accrual is intended, drop the term from the derived line description at 0207:731 — clara._plan_occurrence_basis is #653-owned and pinned, so it cannot vary it — and name the per-occurrence term as a residual in the report.

findings.what: `method` is recorded on the accrual row and never applied anywhere: no lane reads clara.accrual_adjustments at all, and the posted amount comes solely from the frozen revision basis. All four selection rules therefore post identically, while the form labels the control "How each period's amount is chosen" and offers "The amount the previous period recorded".
findings.evidence: Probe E on clara_652r: two accruals, method={rule:'stated_amount'} and method={rule:'prior_period_amount'}, same stated 120000. Both revisions carry the identical frozen basis and both post primary@2026-06-30=120000, primary@2026-07-31=120000, primary@2026-08-31=120000 — including the FIRST period, where 'the amount the previous period recorded' does not exist. `grep -rn accrual_adjustments packages/db/migrations/*.sql | grep -v 0207` returns nothing; `grep -c accrual packages/runtime/lib/plan-occurrences.mjs` = 0.
findings.fix: Either narrow the enum in this slice to the rule that is actually honoured (`stated_amount`) and name the other three as a successor residual, or keep the enum and say out loud — in the 0207 header, CONTEXT.md's "Calculation method" entry and the form's methodHint — that the rule is recorded for the successor and does not vary what this slice posts. As written the product copy promises per-period amount selection that no code performs.

findings.what: The same-op-key-different-payload conflict surfaces as a bare CLR10 with NO detail, so it carries none of the `detail.reason` the file's own refusal vocabulary promises and the web lane cannot classify or field-map it.
findings.evidence: Probe B2 on clara_652r: replay of one key with cents changed 120000 -> 999 raised `code=CLR10 detail=(none) msg="op_key reused with different args"`, and the footprint stayed {plans:1,revisions:1,occurrences:1,accruals:1,work:2}. The 0207 header's "REFUSAL VOCABULARY THIS FILE OWNS" block and its "INHERITED UNCHANGED" list both omit this case.
findings.fix: Wrap the _reserve_op call in an exception block in both doors and re-raise as CLR10 with detail {"reason":"op_key_conflict"} (or add the token to the header's inherited list and map it in apps/web/lib/accruals + the form's refusal copy), so a preparer sees "this key already configured a different accrual" rather than an unclassified failure.

findings.what: The tail's "this file altered no foreign table" proof for clara.document_service_periods is a transcribed literal (`count(*) <> 14`) rather than a value captured in §0, unlike the six body digests which are captured into the w652_plan_pin temp table and re-compared.
findings.evidence: Line 1364: `if (select count(*)::int from pg_constraint where conrelid='clara.document_service_periods'::regclass) <> 14 then raise ...`. It held on the from-scratch chain (194 migrations applied, exit 0), but it asserts a property of the whole chain below 0207, not of this file: any migration numbered under 0207 that ever adds a constraint to that relation reds the entire chain with a message about this file. #653's 0208 is the wave's declared user of that relation and sits above 0207 today, so the risk is a renumbering away.
findings.fix: Capture the count in §0 into the same temp table (`create temp table w652_foreign_pin as select count(*) ...`) and compare §E against it, exactly as the six plan-lane digests are handled. The assertion then proves what it claims — that THIS file added nothing — independent of the chain below it.

findings.what: Three of the battery's seventeen cells — the reversal binding (p652.reversal.binds), the locked-period catch-up (p652.catchup.locked) and entrance independence (p652.plan.occurrence.typed) — skip themselves when the run day is the last day of its month, so on one day in 31 the ticket's reversal and lock evidence is a counted skip rather than a pass.
findings.evidence: `if (await isMonthEnd()) { t.skip("p652.reversal.binds needs a day that is not the month end…") }` at :428, and the same guard at :486 and :711. My run on 2026-09-17 was 17/17 pass / 0 skip; on 2026-09-30 it would be 17/14/3. WORK-ORDER rule 10: "skipped batteries are not evidence".
findings.fix: Shape those three cells' schedules with `dayRule:'day_of_month', dayOfMonth:15` instead of `last_day_of_month` — the scenario "an accrual admitted, its reversal outstanding" then exists on every calendar day and the guard can be deleted.

findings.what: The ⌘K keyword "accruals" is REMOVED from the existing `plans` row rather than only added to the new `accruals` row — a behaviour change to a shipped surface inside a shared file the brief did not assign to this ticket.
findings.evidence: `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- apps/web/lib/command/routes.ts`: `- plans: { id: "registersPlans", keywords: ["plans", "adjustments", "accruals", "registers"] }` / `+ plans: { id: "registersPlans", keywords: ["plans", "adjustments", "registers"] }`.
